design.md:2742-2895 Security Boundaries names every trust boundary this feature crosses (CLI-misuse/disabled-legacy guard; staged-artifact-to-live-path publication boundary; protected-file/approval-sidecar non-participation boundary; dependency-subprocess-stderr leak boundary), states the mechanism at each (fail-closed Block, journaled atomic commit, guard-invariants.json suffix reservation, canonical-detail construction), addresses data classification (no credential/PII ever read; explicit no-clock/no-network/no-Provider-API statement) and OWASP-adjacent concerns (injection via raw stderr text forbidden, M8; path-traversal/protected-write via guard-invariants.json suffix match). The one substantive content change under review on its merits -- the AC-059 approval-surface write-scope lock and its 2026-08-28 sequencing correction (design.md:2764-2795) -- is internally sound: it correctly identifies that T-007 (owner) authors only resolve-project-context.* while validate-resolver-evidence.* is authored by the downstream T-008, and resolves this by splitting discharge into (a) T-007 registering and running the grep over the scripts that exist at its own gate, and (b) relying on the registered check being CI-gated (re-executed on every subsequent commit, not a one-shot verification) to automatically cover the second glob once T-008's files land -- a mechanism already established and previously passed for AC-025 (identical grep, same script set, same cadence), so no new suite or task obligation is introduced (design.md:2775-2777, matching acceptance-tests.md AC-059/TEST-059 and requirements.md AC-059 verbatim). This reasoning is corroborated by investigation.md's 'Ruling E's own repair' section, which records the same fix with commit 94704f9c and matches the current design.md digest. One minor imprecision noted, not blocking: design.md:2792 analogizes the mechanism to 'AC-032/AC-033/AC-034 bind[ing] every task's commits without per-task re-verification', but AC-032 (requirements.md:950) is a one-time constraint on this Phase-1 spec package's own already-closed commits and AC-033 (requirements.md:951) explicitly requires each future task to carry its own CHANGELOG entry (i.e. is per-task-verified, not exempt from re-verification) -- only AC-034's repository-wide grep is a true structural analogue. This does not undermine the correction's core claim, which rests on AC-025's own already-passed identical mechanism, not on the AC-032/033 citations.
